Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the StellarTech Solutions Second Quarter Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today's call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Emily Carter, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter, VP of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and welcome to StellarTech Solutions’ second quarter earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Chen, CEO; David Lee, CFO; and Michael Wong, CTO.
Earlier today, we published our earnings press release and presentation, which are available on our Investor Relations site. Today’s discussion may include forward-looking statements. With that, let me turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Emily, and welcome everyone.

We’re pleased with our performance this quarter. I want to highlight a few areas. First, turning to our wafer ASP performance. We observed a 3% increase in overall wafer ASP compared to Q1 2020. This translates to an overall ASP of approximately $1,236 per wafer, up from roughly $1,200 in the previous quarter. The key driver was the surge in 28nm revenue shipments. This segment experienced a substantial 12% increase in wafer ASP quarter-over-quarter, reaching approximately $850 per wafer. This jump is attributable to a higher proportion of 28nm wafers dedicated to high-performance computing (HPC) applications and advanced connectivity solutions (5G infrastructure), specifically for RF front-end modules and baseband processors. Strong demand across multiple sectors, including IoT devices, automotive microcontrollers (especially those supporting advanced driver-assistance systems - ADAS), and consumer electronics, created a degree of capacity tightness within our 28nm production lines, allowing for some strategic price adjustments.

Also, our second quarter consolidated revenue reached NT$44.39 billion, a healthy 5% increase quarter-over-quarter compared to Q1 2020 revenue of NT$42.28 billion. This growth is attributable to both Average Selling Price (ASP) Improvement and Wafer Shipment Volume Growth. We observed a blended ASP increase of approximately 3% across our core product lines, primarily driven by increased demand for our higher-margin, advanced node wafers used in 5G infrastructure and high-performance computing (HPC) applications. Alongside ASP improvements, we also witnessed a 2% increase in overall wafer shipment volume.

Finally, I want to mention our Texas Instruments' Long-Term Agreement (LTA) with UMC. In Q3 2024, we recognized underutilization charges of $47 million related to the UMC LTA. This represents a 22% increase compared to the $38.5 million recognized in Q2 2024 and a 15% decrease compared to the $55 million recognized in Q3 2023. This was driven by demand softness in the industrial and automotive segments, and our shifting product mix.

I’ll now pass it over to David Lee to walk through the numbers in more detail.

David Lee, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Sarah, and hello, everyone.

Let me break it down starting with our Texas Instruments' Long-Term Agreement (LTA) with UMC. Several factors contributed to this quarter's underutilization charges. While our automotive segment demonstrated resilience with a 4% sequential revenue increase, the industrial segment experienced a more pronounced slowdown. Specifically, programmable logic controllers and factory automation segments saw weaker-than-expected demand, resulting in lower wafer starts at UMC. The industrial sector's overall contribution to the underutilization charges is estimated at approximately 60%. We are strategically shifting our product mix towards higher-margin, more advanced products. This naturally leads to a temporary reduction in demand for products manufactured on the 28nm and 40nm nodes, which are prominent in our UMC LTA. We are actively pursuing several strategies to mitigate the impact of underutilization charges and optimize our LTA with UMC, including enhancing our demand forecasting models to improve the accuracy of our capacity planning, and working closely with our engineering teams to identify opportunities to re-design products to utilize capacity on the UMC nodes with higher utilization rates. We expect the underutilization charges to stabilize in Q4 2024, projecting a range of $42 million to $48 million.

Now, moving to our net margin and Diluted EPS (earnings per share) results, which we’ve been tracking closely. Acme Tech Solutions demonstrated a strong financial performance in the second quarter of 2024. Net income attributable to the stockholder of the parent company reached NT$6.68 billion, translating to a robust 15.1% net income margin. Diluted earnings per share (EPS) stood at NT$0.55, a substantial improvement compared to the NT$0.19 reported in Q1 2023. This represents a year-over-year increase of approximately 189%, indicating a significant turnaround in profitability. Q2 revenue reached NT$44.24 billion, a 22% increase compared to the NT$36.26 billion reported in Q2 2023. This growth was primarily fueled by strong demand for Acme Tech Solutions' cloud-based security solutions and its newly launched AI-powered analytics platform. Gross margin improved to 42.5% in Q2, up from 39.8% in Q2 2023, due to strategic sourcing, manufacturing efficiencies, and a product mix shift.

Lastly, I'd like to briefly touch on our overall wafer ASP comments, and the by node or segment wafer ASP comments for this quarter. We anticipate wafer ASP in U.S. dollar to remain relatively flat in Q3 2020. We expect the exceptional growth in 28nm to moderate in Q3 as capacity catches up with demand. While demand will remain strong, the pricing pressure will likely ease, leading to a stabilization of ASP in this segment. We foresee continued downward pressure on 16nm/12nm ASP due to increasing competition. The continued ramp-up of 5nm production will have a positive impact on overall ASP, but its effect will be partially offset by the factors mentioned above. We are projecting roughly 15% of our revenue to come from 5nm by the end of Q3.

Now, let me hand things over to Michael Wong to talk about product and operational progress.

Michael Wong, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, David.

This was a busy quarter for our teams. On the innovation front, we made meaningful advances around our sales by segment or platforms, their respective margin levels, and their respective management comments. The Communication segment generated $4.8 billion in revenue for Q3 2023, representing a 5% decrease year-over-year. This decline is primarily attributed to increased competitive pressure in the enterprise unified communications platform space, particularly from newer cloud-native solutions. Within the Communication segment, our cloud-based collaboration platform, "ConnectNow," saw a respectable 8% increase in subscriptions. However, this growth wasn't sufficient to offset the declines in our hardware and traditional software offerings. The Computer segment saw a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year, reaching $2.3 billion. This growth was driven by strong demand for our high-performance computing (HPC) solutions targeting the AI and machine learning markets. The Computer segment's gross margin improved significantly to 48%, up from 45% in Q3 2022. Our "Other" segments, encompassing areas such as IoT solutions and professional services, collectively generated $2.4 billion in revenue, representing a 10% increase year-over-year.

Also worth noting is our improvement in gross margin results, QoQ changes, YoY changes with reasons, Gross margin results v.s. guidance from last quarter with reasons. Our analysis reveals a significant improvement in gross margin for the second quarter of 2024. The reported gross margin of 23.1% represents a substantial 26% sequential increase compared to the 18.3% reported in Q1 2024. Furthermore, on a year-over-year basis, this represents a notable improvement of 350 basis points compared to the 19.6% gross margin reported in Q2 2023. The impressive 26% QoQ jump in gross margin can be attributed to a confluence of factors, primarily centered around product mix optimization, manufacturing cost efficiencies, and ongoing cost reduction initiatives. In Q1, sales were heavily weighted towards our entry-level "Atlas" product line. In Q2, we witnessed a significant shift. Demand for our higher-margin "Titan" and "Zenith" product lines increased, leading to a more profitable overall revenue profile.

And we’ve made foundational changes in how we approach revenue results, QoQ changes, YoY changes with reasons, revenue results v.s. guidance from last quarter with reasons. Looking at the first six months of 2020, our consolidated revenue reached NT$86.6 billion, a substantial 26% increase compared to the same period in 2019 (YoY). USJC contributed approximately 10%, or NT$8.66 billion, to our topline in H1 2020. The global rollout of 5G infrastructure continues to drive demand for our advanced node wafers. The increasing demand for HPC solutions, driven by AI, machine learning, and data analytics, is also fueling growth. In our Q1 2020 earnings call, we guided for Q2 revenue to be in the range of NT$43.5 billion to NT$44.5 billion. Our actual revenue of NT$44.39 billion falls within this range, but at the higher end. This was due to accelerated 5G rollout in select markets, stronger-than-expected HPC demand, and favorable currency exchange rates.

Let’s now open the floor for questions.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
Hi, thanks for taking my question. On gross margin results, QoQ changes, YoY changes with reasons, Gross margin results  v.s. guidance from last quarter with reasons, could you expand on what’s driving that strength?

Sarah Chen:
Certainly. As Michael touched upon, the impressive 26% QoQ jump in gross margin can be attributed to a confluence of factors, primarily centered around product mix optimization, manufacturing cost efficiencies, and ongoing cost reduction initiatives. Specifically, the ASP for Titan increased 5% QoQ due to bundled software offerings, adding to the margin impact. Our fabrication facilities experienced higher capacity utilization rates in Q2 compared to Q1, resulting in a significant reduction in the fixed cost allocated per wafer. We also saw benefits from our ongoing cost reduction activities, including supply chain optimization, energy efficiency programs, and automation enhancements.

Analyst 2:
A follow-up on net margin and Diluted EPS (earnings per share) results. How confident are you that you can maintain this level of profitability going forward?

David Lee:
We are cautiously optimistic about our ability to sustain and even slightly improve our net margin in the coming quarters. We anticipate continued revenue growth driven by our cloud security and AI analytics segments. We are also committed to maintaining tight control over operating expenses and driving further efficiencies across the organization. We are projecting Q3 revenue to reach NT$48 billion, with a net income margin of 15.5%. EPS is expected to be in the range of NT$0.60 to NT$0.65. Of course, we are closely monitoring global economic conditions and geopolitical risks, but we are confident in our ability to navigate these challenges and deliver strong financial performance.

Analyst 3:
And for sales by segment or platforms, their respective margin levels, and their respective management comments, any update on the strategic initiatives to address the challenges in the Communication segment?

Michael Wong:
Yes, absolutely. As Sarah mentioned earlier, we are aggressively investing in ConnectNow's feature set, focusing on AI-powered productivity tools and enhanced security features to differentiate our offering. We are also exploring strategic partnerships to expand our reach in the SMB market with a revamped MessagePro offering. We are accelerating our transition to cloud-based solutions across all segments. This includes investing in the development of new cloud-native applications, migrating existing solutions to the cloud, and offering hybrid cloud deployment options.

Analyst 4:
Just a final one — on customer LTA (Long Term Agreement) or supply agreement update, and the underutilization charges for this quarter, is the improvement mostly due to the cost-cutting measures implemented?

David Lee:
The cost-cutting measures certainly played a role, but it's more nuanced than that. We are enhancing our demand forecasting models to improve the accuracy of our capacity planning, and working closely with our engineering teams to identify opportunities to re-design products to utilize capacity on the UMC nodes with higher utilization rates. We maintain a strong working relationship with UMC, and we are in continuous discussions with them to explore options for optimizing the LTA, including potential adjustments to the committed capacity levels and pricing structure. This might involve renegotiating specific volume commitments based on revised demand forecasts. We are also exploring strategic partnerships with other companies that may be able to utilize the reserved capacity at UMC under certain conditions, subject to UMC's approval and our internal policies.

Closing

Sarah Chen:
Thank you again for joining us today. We remain confident in our long-term growth story and are committed to disciplined execution. We appreciate your continued interest and support.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes today’s call. You may now disconnect.
